sovereign_country.strategic_role: 12.5%统一企业税、CySEC外汇券商牌照与游戏发行业务

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale International Distribution of Acetate Eyeglass Frames

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English-Common-Law foundation with EU/civil-law statutory overlay; unitary national jurisdiction without sub-state tax distinction)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cyprus Companies Law, Cap. 113, as amended (incorporation and registration provisions; Memorandum and Articles of Association; registered office; directors and company secretary), supplemented by the Companies (Amendment) Laws 2015-2023 and the Companies (Fees) Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOROC), Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Nicosia, Cyprus (Ariadne electronic filing portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&A) together with the Application for Registration of a Private Limited Company and Statement of Compliance, filed electronically through the Ariadne company registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for private limited companies under the Cyprus Companies Law, Cap. 113; one subscriber share must be taken (standard practice: 1,000 ordinary shares of EUR 1.00 each). No escrow account, bank certificate or paid-up capital deposit is required at incorporation; capital duty abolished as from 1 January 2016.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Department of Taxation, Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Cyprus; online portal: https://taxportal.mof.gov.cy
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation with the Registrar of Companies (Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver), the Cyprus Tax Department automatically registers the company for income tax purposes and issues a Tax Identification Code (TIC). For VAT, a separate VAT registration application must be submitted electronically through the Tax Portal or via Form VAT 1 to the District VAT Office where the registered office is located. Foreign entities without local incorporation must apply for a Cyprus tax identification number via Form TIC 100 and, if required, VAT registration upon first taxable transaction or upon exceeding the VAT threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election is available under Cyprus law. Cyprus entities are taxed at entity level. Optional group VAT registration is available for related companies. Hybrid mismatch rules apply under EU ATAD Directive (Cyprus Income Tax Law, Section 21A) and must be disclosed in the Cyprus tax return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) under the Value Added Tax Law of 2000 (N.95(I)/2000), as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €15,600 annual taxable turnover for locally established businesses; €35,000 for distance sales of goods to Cyprus from other EU Member States
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Cyprus does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping. Standard e-invoicing (e.g., PDF, e-mail) is accepted. VAT returns must be submitted electronically via the Tax Portal, with periodic VIES statements for intra-EU supplies. No API-based continuous transaction control is currently enforced.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to supplies of goods dispatched or transported by the supplier, the customer, or a third party to a destination outside the EU, provided the goods leave the EU within 3 months of the supply and documentary evidence is retained. Offshore services supplied to a business customer established outside Cyprus and outside the EU may be zero-rated under Article 84 of the Cyprus VAT Law. Services directly related to exported goods (e.g., transport, handling) also qualify.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EU Single Administrative Document – SAD) with exit certificate
Bill of Lading / CMR / Air Waybill evidencing transportation to outside the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer proof showing payment in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Cyprus VAT authorities may audit zero-rated export claims retrospectively for 6 years. Where zero-rating is wrongly claimed, VAT becomes immediately assessable together with interest at the statutory rate and administrative penalties under the Assessment and Collection of Taxes Law (N.4/1978). Deliberate or fraudulent claims may trigger penalties up to 100% of the tax due, criminal prosecution, and removal from the VAT register with reputational harm.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Cyprus (Kentriki Trapeza tis Kyprou), the national competent authority within the European System of Central Banks and the Single Supervisory Mechanism, acting in coordination with the Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC) for payment, clearing, and derivative market oversight
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union; Cyprus has no exchange-control regime on either the current account or the capital account. The euro (EUR) is legal tender, and profit remittance, dividend distribution, and liquidation proceeds may be freely paid to non-resident shareholders without central bank approval and without Cyprus dividend withholding tax, subject only to anti-money-laundering source-of-funds verification at the paying bank and to the absence of artificial arrangements that constitute abuse under EU anti-avoidance principles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio or timeline for export receipts. A Cyprus incorporated exporter may retain 100 percent of export proceeds in EUR or in any foreign currency account indefinitely. The sole administrative duty is indirect: the servicing commercial bank automatically reports cross-border transactions to the Central Bank of Cyprus for balance-of-payments statistics under ECB Regulation (EU) No 184/2014, with the standard general reporting threshold of EUR 12,500 per individual transfer instruction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account paired with a Capital Escrow Account for share capital receipts
Operational Account paired with a Trade Settlement and Import Letter of Credit sub-ledger
Operational Account with dedicated EUR, USD, and GBP sub-accounts
Operational Account with hybrid remote onboarding eligibility for low-risk EU corporates

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, with strict legal constraints. An EU-authorised Electronic Money Institution (EMI) may legally passport into Cyprus under PSD2 and the E-Money Directive and may hold accounts for the Cypriot company without a physical branch. By contrast, a UK, US, or other offshore EMI without a valid EU passport cannot onboard the Cyprus entity unless it holds an EU authorisation, establishes a Cyprus branch, or uses an EU-licensed sponsor. In addition, funds held with an EMI are not covered by the Cypriot Depositor Protection Scheme, and external SWIFT settlements of the EMI may be delayed because the EMI relies on downstream bank correspondent accounts. Consequently, EMIs are best used as secondary collection and Platform_Pay rails for e-commerce and wholesale card receipts, not as the primary treasury bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 Cypriot banks require at least one physical appearance of the directors and ultimate beneficial owners for the origination interview; fully remote account opening is not accepted for non-resident corporate clients under the Prevention and Suppression of Money Laundering Activities Law (Law 188(I)/2007 as amended) and the Central Bank of Cyprus AML Directive made thereunder. A limited hybrid procedure is available at some banks in which the initial know-your-customer meeting is held by video conference and is followed by a notarised and apostilled identification execution pack couriered to the branch. In practice, a Cyprus-resident registered agent with certified powers of attorney can complete the transaction banking mandates, but the account is activated only after a satisfactory compliance call with the bank's Money Laundering Compliance Officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: ultimate ownership held through a chain of intermediate holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and full Register of Members, written confirmation of each natural-person UBO holding 25 percent or more, corporate ownership diagram across the full holding chain, current Beneficial Ownership Register confirmation filing, certified passport copies of all directors of every intermediate entity, and signed authorisation letters for each holding layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds uncertainty for the initial capital injection into the Cyprus company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorising capitalisation, bank statements of the funding shareholder for the preceding 6 to 12 months, notarised share subscription or shareholder loan agreement, share certificates issued after allotment, tax clearance certificates from the shareholder's country of residence, and a net-worth declaration supported by sale deeds, dividend vouchers, or audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of commercial substance in Cyprus and management-and-control risk for a wholesale trader
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office lease agreement, administrative and secretarial employment contracts, Cyprus VAT and tax registration certificates, board meeting minutes held in Cyprus evidencing strategic decisions, projected profit and loss accounts, warehouse or distribution agency agreements, and evidence of physical inventory flows routed through or documented in Cyprus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment flows to higher-risk East Asian optical-frame suppliers (China and Hong Kong)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Final commercial invoices and purchase orders, packing lists, transport documents (bill of lading or airway bill), customs declarations, supplier sanction-screening reports from reputed databases, audited back-to-back sales contracts with downstream EU buyers, and a written trade-flow narrative approved by the bank's Trade Finance department.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder or intra-group equity is wired via SWIFT MT103, or by SEPA Credit Transfer for euro-area originators, to the Capital Escrow Account. The remittance information field must quote the board resolution number and the Cyprus Companies Registry registration number and must identify the nature of the funds as share subscription, share premium, or shareholder loan so that the receiving bank can assign the correct balance-of-payments statistical classification. No exchange-control permit is required. The bank requires the pre-wire source-of-funds dossier; after the share allotment form is filed with the Registrar of Companies, the funds are released to the operational account. Inbound transfers above the statistical threshold are reported automatically by the bank to the Central Bank of Cyprus.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 and MT202 for regular supplier telegraphic transfers in EUR, USD, GBP, or CNH, with the remittance information referencing the commercial invoice; (2) Commercial letters of credit (sight and 60 to 90 day usance) issued via MT700 for large acetate-frame purchase orders, payable against commercial invoice, packing list, and bill of lading; (3) documentary collections on a documents-against-payment or documents-against-acceptance basis for lower-value orders; and (4) SEPA Instant transfers routed through an EU-linked EMI for refunds and small platform settlements. Each disbursement is matched electronically to the underlying purchase order and invoice through the bank's trade document portal to satisfy AML and sanctions screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX Forwards in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF for covered trade payables and receivables with tenors normally up to 12 months
Open-market Foreign Exchange Swaps (FX-swaps) for liquidity bridging between USD-denominated receipts and the EUR operating account
Offshore CNY Non-Deliverable Forwards (CNH NDFs) on the offshore Chinese market to hedge USD/CNH supplier invoices where onshore CNY delivery is impracticable
Cross-Currency Swaps for refinancing or asset-liability alignment on multi-currency intra-group loans
European-style FX Options (plain vanilla calls and puts) on EUR/USD and EUR/GBP, executed only with the corporate treasury bank as protection against adverse budgeted exchange-rate movements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return / Company Confirmation Statement (Form HE32, Cyprus Companies Law, Cap. 113)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR), Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 days after the company's 'return date'; default return date is the anniversary of incorporation. Once filed, the next return date is the following anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is a criminal offence under Companies Law, Cap. 113; the company and every defaulting officer are liable to statutory fines. Persistent default for two consecutive years may cause the Registrar to issue a warning and administratively strike off the company. DRCOR withholds certificates of good standing and certified extracts while the return remains outstanding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Levy (Annual Government Levy under Companies Law, Cap. 113, s. 148A)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June of each calendar year; applies to every Cyprus private limited company regardless of business activity.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If unpaid by 30 June, an additional late levy of EUR 50 is imposed (total EUR 100, approximately USD 108). Non-payment for two consecutive years gives the Registrar power to strike off the company and cancel its registration; registrations and certificates are blocked until the levy is settled.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Annual Confirmation (Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Ownership via ARIADNI electronic platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR), UBO Registry (ARIADNI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the anniversary of the initial UBO declaration, or after the immediately preceding annual confirmation; any change in beneficial ownership occurring through a share transfer must be reported separately within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual confirmation is a statutory offence under the Cyprus Prevention and Suppression of Money Laundering Activities Law; the company and responsible officers face administrative and criminal fines, including daily default penalties. Repeated or persistent default may lead to the Registrar refusing to issue certificates, flagging the company, and ultimately placing it on the administrative strike-off list.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is mandatory unless the company qualifies for the Cyprus small-company audit exemption under Companies Law, Cap. 113. A private company is exempt only if, for the relevant financial year, it satisfies all of the following: annual turnover does not exceed EUR 70,000; balance-sheet total does not exceed EUR 350,000; average number of employees during the year does not exceed 5; and the company is not a member of a group required to prepare consolidated audited accounts. If any of these ceilings is exceeded, an independent certified public accountant must be appointed to audit the annual financial statements. A wholesale optical-frame distribution company exceeding these limits must therefore procure a statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards as endorsed by the European Union (EU-IFRS), required under Cyprus Companies Law, Cap. 113; financial statements must present a true and fair view and are prepared on a going-concern basis using accrual accounting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Cyprus Companies Law and the Cyprus UBO Register framework, each Cyprus private limited company must maintain an accurate UBO register and file an annual confirmation at least once every 12 months. The annual confirmation is due within 14 days after the anniversary of the initial UBO declaration or the last annual confirmation. Any share transfer that changes the beneficial ownership structure must be reported separately within 30 days of the transfer, and the UBO register must be updated before the annual confirmation can be accepted. The protocol applies irrespective of whether the transfer occurs between non-resident beneficial owners.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholders' general meetings
Minute Book of directors' board meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $540 – $1,620 per annum (EUR 500 – EUR 1,500 for registered office and company secretary services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $1,080 – $2,700 per audit cycle (EUR 1,000 – EUR 2,500 for a small or medium optical-frame wholesale company; higher for consolidated or group accounts)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory rate 12.5%; Notional Interest Deduction (NID) on new equity capital; IP Box regime granting 80% deduction on qualifying IP profits (effective 2.5%); withholding tax exemption on participating dividend distributions; no capital gains tax on disposal of shares except immovable property; group loss relief and group interest restrictions context-dependent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 (Company Tax Return) submitted electronically via the Cyprus Tax Department's Tax For All (TFA) e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, the return is due by 31 December of the following year. Provisional tax installments are typically due on 31 July and 31 December of the tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company registration data: legal name, HE77 registration number, registered office address, tax identification code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Cyprus company's details; non-resident shareholder identity is not entered on the IR4 itself but must be reflected in the Cyprus beneficial ownership register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period and tax year covered: start date and end date in DD/MM/YYYY format.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Cyprus entity's statutory accounting period; do not consolidate non-resident parent accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover, sales, and other operating revenue from wholesale distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all income attributable to the Cyprus resident company's wholesale activities; exclude unrelated parent company sales routed through the Cyprus entity without economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable business expenses: cost of goods sold, logistics, storage, sales commissions, marketing, administrative and financing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses supported by valid invoices, bank evidence, and arm's length transfer pricing documentation for cross-border procurement from related suppliers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chargeable income after disallowed expenditures, capital allowances, IP Box deductions, Notional Interest Deduction, and other statutory reliefs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute on the basis of Cyprus worldwide income for a Cyprus tax-resident company; if non-resident deemed due to central management elsewhere, attach explanation and treaty position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss relief utilized from prior years (maximum five years carryforward).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Cyprus loss carryforward rules to the Cyprus entity's own losses; losses of non-resident related parties are not automatically usable on the IR4.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computation at the statutory rate of 12.5% on chargeable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm no shareholder-level imputation; the tax liability is that of the Cyprus limited company only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, withholding tax credits, and treaty reliefs claimed by the Cyprus company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach certificate of tax residence and credit evidence if claiming relief under a double tax agreement; non-resident shareholders do not claim on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund due after provisional tax payments and withheld taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle payment using the Cyprus company's tax ID; avoid payments from unrelated third-party or opaque accounts because AML checks apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration and signature by an authorized director or statutory auditor.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident director may sign only if lawfully appointed and authorized; the signer assumes personal responsibility for the accuracy of the return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form IR4 attracts an automatic penalty of EUR 100 plus EUR 0.50 per day of delay, capped at EUR 10,000. Late payment of assessed tax attracts annual interest at 5%; inaccurate or fraudulent returns can lead to 100% civil penalties and criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% – Cyprus does not impose withholding tax on dividends paid by a Cyprus resident company to non-resident shareholders; dividend distributions qualifying under the participation exemption are likewise exempt from Cyprus income tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit to the Cyprus paying company: (i) a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the treaty partner's tax authority, (ii) a completed DTA entitlement/beneficial ownership declaration, and (iii) evidence of no misuse of treaty provisions. The Cyprus company applies the DTA rate at source; if excess withholding has occurred, a refund claim is filed with the Cyprus Tax Department within applicable limitation periods.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: 0% on outbound dividends; 15% on interest paid to non-residents not connected with a Cyprus PE; 10% on royalties paid to non-residents (5% for copyright and film/television rights). Treaty rates under Cyprus's DTAs commonly reduce interest and royalty withholding to 0%–10%, subject to beneficial ownership and substance requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Annual related-party transactions exceeding EUR 2,000,000 trigger mandatory Local File documentation; Master File is required for multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000, aligned with OECD Country-by-Country reporting thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Cyprus has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations register like the UAE; however, the Cyprus Tax Department and the EU anti-avoidance framework require genuine management and control, physical premises, qualified employees, real business activities, and actual board decisions in Cyprus. Failure to satisfy economic substance may erode treaty protection, attract CFC attribution, trigger ATAD anti-abuse rules, and cause the company to be treated as tax resident elsewhere.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting wholesale turnover, fabricating purchase invoices for eyeglass frames, inflating cost of sales through circular shell-invoice flows, or misdeclaring IP Box eligibility to reduce chargeable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty up to 100% of the tax evaded plus 5% annual interest; criminal conviction for tax fraud carrying fines up to EUR 100,000 and imprisonment up to five years; loss of reliefs and carryforward losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who authorizes or participates in fraudulent filing is jointly and severally liable for the company's tax debts; the corporate veil may be pierced, and the director faces travel bans, asset freezes, disqualification, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting the wholesale mark-up for frame distribution below arm's length, failing to prepare contemporaneous TP documentation, non-filing of the IR4, or using related-party loans with excessive interest rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment to arm's length profit; disallowance of excessive deductions; penalties of up to 100% of the additional assessed tax; late filing penalties up to EUR 10,000; possible interest on underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve deficient TP policies without reasonable economic analysis can be held personally liable for resulting tax deficiencies and penalties if they have breached fiduciary duties; disqualification and negative credit sanctions apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Cyprus limited company with no office, no employees, no board meetings in Cyprus, and no distribution risk or operational control while all key decisions and cash-flows are managed from a non-resident jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-determination of tax residence; denial of DTA benefits; CFC income attribution in the shareholder's jurisdiction; TP re-characterization; strike-off or dissolution under the Cyprus Companies Law; revocation of tax residency certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for wrongful declarations and abuse of corporate form; authorities may impose civil restitution, asset freeze, travel bans, and where deceptive conduct is proven, custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving settlement funds for ophthalmic frames through Swift_TT or platform payments from sanctioned distributors, processing counterfeit or stolen merchandise transactions, or failing to perform customer due diligence and UBO verification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to five years under Cyprus AML Law 188(I)/2007; freezing orders, confiscation of funds, and cancellation of banking relationships.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally exposed to civil liability and criminal sanctions where they knowingly or recklessly permit money laundering; travel bans, disqualification, and asset restrictions are routinely imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repeated failure to submit provisional tax declarations or Form IR4 by statutory deadlines, or persistent underpayment of provisional tax to fund distributions to shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic penalties of EUR 100 plus daily surcharges capped at EUR 10,000; additional assessment at the discretion of the Commissioner; interest at 5% per annum on unpaid tax; limitation on claiming loss relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who cause such defaults may be personally liable for the penalties if they have acted in breach of their statutory duties; repeated non-compliance can lead to travel bans, director disqualification, and in aggravated cases contempt-of-court imprisonment.
